subject: Marketplace private offer: unit-price mapping & next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@stratos.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Marketplace private offer: unit-price mapping & next steps

Hi Sara — thanks for taking time today. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on: 

Call recap (high level)
- Use case: large-scale document understanding + retrieval-augmented generation for customer support (~70% of tokens are generation).
- Current footprint: ~300M tokens/mo today, expected to ramp to ~750–900M tokens/mo by Q4 with new features.
- Priority: predictable unit economics ($/1M tokens) on AWS Marketplace private offer.

What we discussed and next asks from StratosAI
- Confirm committed monthly floor (you mentioned ~250–350M/mo initial).
- Target blended effective spend you want (you said ~$600–800 per 1M tokens effective to Redwood).
- Procurement contact for formal PO/private-offer setup: you mentioned procure@stratos.ai.

Our mapping notes (for procurement team)
- Baseline: hosted list price equivalent (for comparison) = $1,000 per 1M tokens (this is list, before marketplace fees/markups).
- Marketplace private offer flow: AWS charges take + reseller markup; to deliver an effective $700 per 1M to Redwood we recommend a listed private-offer price of ~$1,000–1,100 per 1M so the marketplace margin is covered.
- Proposed commercial starting point (internal):
  • 0–500M tokens/mo: $800 per 1M (effective to Redwood)
  • 500M+ tokens/mo: $650 per 1M (effective to Redwood)
  • Commitment term: 12 months with quarterly usage reporting and a 30‑day ramp clause.

Attachments: I attached a draft mapping sheet (redwood_private-offer-mapping.xlsx) that shows sample calculations converting list price -> marketplace list -> Redwood effective. Also attached quick CSV with the tier breakpoints (redwood_ratecard-ppu.csv) and a procurement template.

Requested next steps
1) Please confirm the budget band you want us to aim for (you suggested $600–800 per 1M).
2) Confirm procurement contact and whether Stratos requires SLO language (throughput/latency) in the PO.
3) If yes to (2), we will loop in our product/ops to produce an SLO appendix.

If this looks right I can share a HubSpot deal + DocuSign pre-reqs and have our legal/procurement partner draft the private offer.

Thanks — Karthik
--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Lead, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@stratos.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procure@stratos.ai>
Date: 2026-07-12T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer: unit-price mapping & next steps

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap and the workbook. A few quick confirmations from our side: 

- Committed volume: we can commit to a 12‑month term starting at 300M tokens/mo and include step-ups to 600M (Q3) and 900M (Q4) assuming performance and SLOs look good.
- Budget band: our FP&A team is targeting an effective spend in the $650–750 per 1M tokens range (net to vendor). The $600 floor is aggressive but not impossible if we push other internal credits.
- Procurement: please loop in procurement@stratos.ai for contract routing. They will need the private-offer list price, PO template, and a short SLO appendix.

Two asks from us: 
1) Can you provide a 1‑page appendix that maps the private-offer list price to the effective Redwood rate (shows marketplace fees and an example invoice)? That will speed procurement approval.
2) We will want a clause that guarantees a baseline throughput (p95 latency requirement for generation endpoints) or a credit mechanism if you can't meet the committed throughput. Is that something you can include?

If you can send the 1‑pager and the procurement template I’ll start the internal approval. Happy to hop on a quick 20m call with procurement next week.

Best,
Sara
Sara Liu
Head of Platform Partnerships
StratosAI
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@stratos.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-13T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer: unit-price mapping & next steps

Sara / Karthik — jumping in with a few pragmatic notes from pricing/ops side: 

- Marketplace math: AWS Marketplace often adds a ~20–30% pass-through/cover for listing + payment fees depending on channel. That is why Karthik's suggested list->effective delta sits in the $1,000–1,100 per 1M range to hit an effective $700.
- Recommendation: offer a two-tier private-offer with explicit step-up thresholds (Karthik’s suggested 0–500M and 500M+ bands). We can also do a blended average if Stratos prefers a single line item for the PO.
- SLO: we can provide an SLO appendix for p95 generation latency and a credit schedule tied to throughput breaches. Our Ops team has a standard SLO appendix we can attach — I’ve requested it and attached the procurement_template.docx here.
- HubSpot & finance: I will open the HubSpot deal RDW-2026-1783 and attach the mapping workbook. Finance prefers we lock the initial committed spend and publish the private-offer list price in the PO so the marketplace team can create the offer.

Action items from Redwood ops/pricing:
- Karthik: finalize the 1‑pager mapping (list -> marketplace -> effective) and share DocuSign/PO template.
- Marissa: once Karthik confirms numbers, can you tag legal to prep the private-offer language?
- Ben: I’ll create the HubSpot record and set a calendar invite for the procurement sync (20m).

Thanks — Ben
--
Ben Carter
Head of GTM Pricing Operations
Redwood Inference
